behavior: Usually solitary; walks slowly through shallow freshwater, bobbing its rear and sometimes trembling a foot to stir prey. Picks prey by sight, probes only occasionally, and may briefly hold its wings raised after landing.
field_marks: Dark olive-brown upperparts neatly spotted with white
Finely streaked gray-brown head, neck, and upper breast above a white belly
Long folded wings and a short, dark-centered tail with pale barred outer feathers
habitat: Quiet freshwater wetlands, especially wooded ponds, stream edges, swamps, bogs, muddy pools, ditches, and flooded fields; generally avoids tidal flats and salt marshes.
